reasons: Deviation classification is correct: the default for undesignated Materials is Type II (IBM/third-party ownership even for works created during the Service performance period), and the only licence back is limited to use/execute/reproduce/display/perform/distribute 'within Customer's Enterprise only' with no modification or sublicensing rights — that fails the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for its business), so this is not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

Redline is actionable and directionally right: it flips the default for Materials created during the Services to Type I (Customer-owned), extends the Type II licence to perpetual/irrevocable with modification, derivative works and sublicensing for Customer's business purposes, and adds an express Customer retention-of-rights sentence for Content, Customer Components and data — matching the rule's redline guidance (reverse the assignment direction / add licence-back / add Customer Data ownership).

No walk-away term is introduced or left standing: no assignment of Customer IP or data to IBM and no joint ownership; IBM retains ownership of its pre-existing platform materials, which the rule permits.

Comment is accurate, concise, in our voice, and correctly states both what changed and the playbook basis; the changed-character ratios (0.43/0.42) reflect the rewrite the rule genuinely requires rather than excessive editing.

Minor, non-disqualifying points to consider: the amended p0082 default now expressly covers only Materials 'created during the Service performance period', leaving no stated default for pre-existing Materials (they still fall under the §7(c) definition, so the gap is benign), and the Customer-data ownership sentence is appended after p0086(d) rather than as a standalone subsection — placement may need tidying, and 'Content'/'Customer Components'/'Services Recipients' should be confirmed as defined terms in this Agreement.
